mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over three months signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST 3mo % change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between the trigger and returns is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for two consecutive months, accompanied by a YoY increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 2%, signals a tight labor market that increases wage inflation and cost pressures, leading to higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for 2 consecutive months AND PAYEMS YoY % change > 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly % change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly above zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 3% during a recession (UNRATE > 5%) signals a monetary policy pivot to easing, which lowers discount rates and supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months, regardless of other conditions, signals deteriorating labor market health and reduces consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly increase of more than 0.3% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based recovery in demand and supply capacity, which boosts earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly % change > 0.3% AND HOUST monthly % change > 0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
